ai.description: This slender, 1.2m snake is tawny-brown with faint, dark crossbands. It features a distinctively blunt, rounded snout and large, prominent eyes with vertical pupils.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Boiga ochracea* is the presence of a distinct, dark, V-shaped or Y-shaped marking on the top of its head.
ai.habitat: The Tawny Cat Snake inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, typically ranging from lowlands up to elevations of approximately 2,000 meters in the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Tawny Cat Snake is primarily nocturnal and arboreal, using its slender body to navigate tree branches while actively hunting for lizards and bird eggs at night.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Tawny Cat Snake is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–12 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Boiga ochracea* is found across the Himalayas, Northeast India, and the Western Ghats, typically inhabiting forested regions from sea level up to 2,000 meters.
